mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discount rates affecting future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 2,000 above the prior month's level is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting labor market strength and investor optimism.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform the average of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (units of housing starts) and GDPC1 (goods orders) show consecutive monthly increases above their prior month's levels, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating robust demand for capital goods and housing.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the mean of 30 such non-consecutive positive signal events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 95 of the prior month's value, in the context of rising UNRATE, predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return due to supply-side weakness and reduced growth expectations.
regime_hint: Supply contraction with rising labor costs
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior month's average (p > 0.05) when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 3%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative as investors anticipate rate hikes and discount future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative effect relative to the 12-month pre-inflation period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 6% for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as lower expected labor costs boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the mean of 20 similar low-unrate regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (housing starts) exceed their prior month's levels by at least 10%, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is predicted to be positive reflecting strong consumer and housing demand.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns do not outperform the average of 10 similar positive signal events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 (goods orders) by more than 10% in a month accompanied by a rise in FEDFUNDS suggests supply contraction and tighter credit, leading to a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline in 10 such contraction events (p > 0.05).
